subject: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: John Alvarez <john.alvarez@shopcraft.io>, ops-team@acme-ops.com
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps

Hi John / ShopCraft ops team,

We’re seeing a partial network connectivity disruption at one of our CloudX edge regions that is intermittently impacting requests routed through EU and APAC POPs. Symptoms: elevated 5xx rates for some customers, increased tail latency, and occasional stream interruptions. CloudX has flagged a peering configuration incident (see status@cloudx.com) and we’re treating this as a high-priority escalation.

Immediate customer-facing mitigations we recommend (actionable now):
- Short-term traffic steering: set your traffic preference to US regions only. For customers using DNS-based steering, reduce DNS TTL to 60s and update the A/ALIAS records to point to the US ingress endpoints listed in our playbook.
- Client-side retries: enable idempotent retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) and set X-Redwood-Fallback: true when accepting lower-throughput fallback model variants.
- Disable TCP keepalive offloads to avoid long-lived stalled connections if you’re behind aggressive NATs.

We’ve attached an interim incident summary and a condensed step-by-step traffic steer playbook (traffic_steer_playbook.md) with exact endpoints and sample curl commands. Internal owners (Marcus) are on capacity checks for US pools; Lauren is coordinating legal/comms.

I’ll follow up with a short timeline and a post-incident call invite once we have containment. If you’d like Redwood to execute the traffic steering for you (we can update your DNS records and coordinate TTLs with your DNS provider), reply with approval and a point of contact.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize minimizing customer impact.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: incident_summary_v1.pdf, traffic_steer_playbook.md

From: John Alvarez <john.alvarez@shopcraft.io>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-14T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the quick note.

A couple quick questions from our side before we proceed:
1) Can you confirm whether ShopCraft’s Private deployment (VPC peering) will be affected by the same CloudX peering event? We have a live VPC setup with Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 and want to know if routing through that lane is safe.
2) If we approve Redwood to manage DNS TTL updates, what GUID/record changes will you make and how long until the new traffic profile is fully shifted?
3) We’ll need logs for our SRE team — attaching a short snippet showing elevated 502s from our end.

If it helps, we can accept an immediate shift to US-only for the next 3 hours to avoid customer-facing errors while you confirm capacity. Please confirm and we’ll give you the go-ahead.

—John
John Alvarez
Site Reliability Engineering Lead | ShopCraft
john.alvarez@shopcraft.io
Attachment: customer_log_snippet.txt

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, John Alvarez <john.alvarez@shopcraft.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-14T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps

Vanessa / John — quick technical update and ask.

On the CloudX incident: their status page indicates a peering flap between EU edge routers and some APAC POPs. For Dedicated and Private customers with explicit VPC peering in us-west-2, traffic should remain internal-to-cloud provider and not be hit by the public peering disruption (confirming: ShopCraft’s Dedicated pools in us-west-2 are available).

Action items I’m initiating now:
- Capacity check: reserving extra US pool slots for ShopCraft for the next 6 hours (will update capacity numbers in 15–20 mins).
- DNS plan: if ShopCraft approves, Redwood will perform the DNS override via your registrar API (we only change the public A/ALIAS for inference.example.shopcraft.com to us-ingress-1.redwood.net). We’ll set TTL=60 and stage a rollback plan.
- Telemetry: enabling 1s sampling for tail latency traces and turning on additional token-level logging for affected customer tokens for the duration of the incident.

Notes on fallback behaviour: when X-Redwood-Fallback: true is used, we route to a smaller model variant that has verified lower GPU memory usage and faster cold-start times. This reduces quality slightly (shorter contexts, more conservative sampling) but avoids 5xx errors while we stabilize.

I’ll post the capacity numbers and a call invite for a 30-min sync in 20.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: John Alvarez <john.alvarez@shopcraft.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps

John — thanks for the log snippet. You have the greenlight from ShopCraft to proceed with US-only traffic steering for the next 3 hours per your note? If yes, reply "approve-traffic-steer" and include the DNS/registrar contact (if any).

I’ll summarize the ask to our operations channel and confirm when the change is live. Here are the concrete next steps so everyone is aligned:
1) Customer approval: John to reply with "approve-traffic-steer" (and any registrar credentials out-of-band).
2) Ops action: Marcus to change public A/ALIAS and set TTL=60, and reserve US pool capacity.
3) Monitoring: increase sampling and watch 5xx rates; Marcus to post live metrics link.
4) Comms: Lauren to prepare a short post-incident email template; we’ll send an update within 2 hours and a formal postmortem within 72 hours.

If you want Redwood to perform the DNS changes, John, we’ll need a two-factor approval (email + short SSO confirmation). If you prefer to do it yourselves, the exact records are in the attached playbook.

Thanks — I’ll open a short incident ticket and a follow-up calendar invite.

Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: traffic_steer_playbook.md

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, John Alvarez <john.alvarez@shopcraft.io>
Date: 2028-01-15T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Regional network interruption — interim traffic steering guidance & next steps

Following up after overnight observation.

Summary: CloudX has contained the peering flap; EU/APAC ingress is recovering but residual packet loss remains and CloudX expects a gradual healing window over 18–36 hours. Marcus confirmed US pool capacity during the containment window and ShopCraft traffic steering was completed at 2028-01-14T11:22:35-08:00. We saw a ~92% drop in your customer-facing 5xxs after the change.

Planned next steps:
- We’ll keep ShopCraft on US-only steering for an additional 6 hours as a conservative buffer.
- Draft postmortem will be shared with legal and SRE for review by EOD 2028-01-16; public-facing summary for affected customers is scheduled for 2028-01-17.
- Lauren will host a 30-min post-incident sync with ShopCraft tomorrow 2028-01-15T12:00PT to review telemetry and credits policy (invite to follow).

Thanks for the quick coordination — we’ll follow up on SLA/credits and include the trace samples you attached.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Note: CloudX status reference: https://status.cloudx.com/incident/78912
